genre.en: pet lifestyle documentary photography: a real home, a real pet doing what it does, candid, warm window light

s: a rabbit nibbles a strand of hay beside the pack on a pale wooden floor, hard morning sun from the window, an olive-green wall behind
loose hay spills from the open pack onto a butter-yellow surface, warm side light catching every strand

a bread-shaped compressed hay bale sits fat and huge in the foreground of a rabbit's wooden hutch floor, its sliced end showing tight green fibers, against a deep terracotta-orange hutch wall, hard morning sun slanting in from the left through the wire door and laying crisp barred shadows across the bale and the floor

the box of timothy hay fills the frame as it rests on a worn wooden shelf in a family living room, a grey-and-white rabbit sitting right beside it with its nose at the open end of the bale, against a muted sea-green wall, one hard window beam from camera right casting a sharp long shadow of the box and the rabbit's ears across the shelf

a split loaf-like hay bale opened and pulled apart in half, one half propped upright, set on a pine pet-room floor against a deep-navy wall, a single hard spotlight from high on the left carving a clear dark shadow behind the bale and showing the dust-free strands

a guinea pig stands on its hind legs pulling a strand from the large hay package set on a bathroom-tile floor beside its cage, against a tomato-red painted wall, hard sun from a side window slicing across the package and throwing a sharp diagonal shadow

the hay bale sits big in the middle of a rabbit's play pen on a wooden floor beside a ceramic water bowl and a chinchilla dust bath, against a mint-green wall, low hard sunlight from the right making long crisp shadows of the bale and the pen bars across the floor
